title.zh: 卷二二 列傳第十四 李元忠 盧文偉 李義深
title.en: Volume 22 Biographies 14: Li Yuanzhong; Lu Wenwei; Li Yishen
title.raw: 卷二二 列傳第十四 李元忠 盧文偉 李義深 Volume 22 Biographies 14: Li Yuanzhong; Lu Wenwei; Li Yishen

sentences.zh: 李元忠 族弟密 族叔景遺 盧文偉 孫詢祖 族人勇 李義深

translations.literal: Li Yuanzhong; younger clansman Mi; clansman uncle Jingyi; Lu Wenwei; Sun Xunzu; clansman Yong; Li Yishen
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong; his younger clansman Mi; his clansman uncle Jingyi; Lu Wenwei; Sun Xunzu; his clansman Yong; and Li Yishen

sentences.zh: 李元忠，趙郡柏人人也。

translations.literal: Li Yuanzhong was a native of Bo in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong came from Bo in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖靈，魏定州刺史、鉅鹿公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ling served in Wei as Governor of Ding Province and Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ling had served in Wei as governor of Ding Province and duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 祖恢，鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was general who guards the west.

sentences.zh: 父顯甫，安州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xianfu was Governor of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianfu was governor of An Province.

sentences.zh: 元忠少厲志操，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: In youth Yuanzhong cultivated resolute integrity and was known for filial piety during mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yuanzhong forged a resolute character and won renown for filial piety in mourning.

sentences.zh: 襲爵平棘子。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Viscount of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title viscount of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 魏清河王懌為司空，辟為士曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yi of Wei became Minister of Works, he recruited Yuanzhong as staff officer in the personnel bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yi of Wei became minister of works, he recruited Yuanzhong as staff officer in the personnel bureau.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉，復啟為長流參軍。

translations.literal: When Yi was transferred to Grand Commandant, he again recommended him as senior itinerant staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was transferred to grand commandant, he again recommended him as senior itinerant staff officer.

sentences.zh: 懌後為太傅，尋被詔為營構明堂大都督，又引為主簿。

translations.literal: Later when Yi became Grand Tutor, he was soon ordered Grand Director-General for the Construction of the Bright Hall, and again took Yuanzhong as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yi became grand tutor, he was soon ordered grand director-general for the construction of the Bright Hall and again took Yuanzhong as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 元忠粗覽史書及陰陽數術，解鼓箏，兼好射彈，有巧思。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong had a rough knowledge of historical works and the arts of yin-yang and numerology; he could play the zither and drum, also loved archery and slingshot, and had ingenious ideas.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong had read widely in history and the arts of yin-yang and numerology. He could play the zither and drum, loved archery and slingshot, and had a gift for invention.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，去任。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left his post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，相州刺史、安樂王鑒請為府司馬，元忠以艱憂，固辭不就。

translations.literal: Before long, Governor of Xiang Province Prince of Anle Jian invited him to be commander in the princely household, but Yuanzhong, in deep mourning, firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Governor of Xiang Province Prince of Anle Jian invited him to serve as commander in the princely household, but Yuanzhong, still in deep mourning, firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 初，元忠以母老多患，乃專心醫藥，研習積年，遂善於方技。

translations.literal: At first, because his mother was old and often ill, Yuanzhong devoted himself to medicine, studying for years until he became skilled in the healing arts.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because his mother was old and often ill, Yuanzhong devoted himself to medicine. He studied for years until he mastered the healing arts.

sentences.zh: 性仁恕，見有疾者，不問貴賤，皆為救療。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and forgiving; whenever he saw the sick, regardless of rank, he treated them.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was benevolent and forgiving. Whenever he saw the sick, high or low, he treated them.

sentences.zh: 家素富實，其家人在鄉，多有舉貸求利，元忠每焚契免責。

translations.literal: The family had long been wealthy; household members in the countryside often made loans at interest, but Yuanzhong repeatedly burned the contracts and released debtors from obligation.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long been wealthy. Household members in the countryside often made loans at interest, but Yuanzhong repeatedly burned the contracts and released the debtors.

sentences.zh: 鄉人甚敬重之。

translations.literal: The people of the district greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the district held him in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 魏孝明時，盜賊蜂起，清河有五百人西戍，還經南趙郡，以路梗共投元忠。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaoming of Wei's reign bandits rose everywhere; five hundred men from Qinghe who had been garrisoned in the west, returning through Southern Zhao Commandery, found the roads blocked and together sought refuge with Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaoming of Wei's reign bandits rose everywhere. Five hundred men from Qinghe, returning from garrison duty in the west through Southern Zhao Commandery, found the roads blocked and together sought refuge with Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 奉絹千疋，元忠唯受一疋，殺五羊以食之，遣奴為導，曰：「若逢賊，但道李元忠遣送。

translations.literal: They presented a thousand bolts of silk; Yuanzhong accepted only one bolt, slaughtered five sheep to feed them, and sent a servant to guide them, saying, "If you meet bandits, simply say Li Yuanzhong sent you on your way.
translations.idiomatic: They presented a thousand bolts of silk. Yuanzhong accepted only one, slaughtered five sheep to feed them, and sent a servant to guide them. "If you meet bandits," he said, "simply tell them Li Yuanzhong sent you on your way.

sentences.zh: 」奴如其言，賊皆捨避。

translations.literal: " The servant did as told, and the bandits all let them pass.
translations.idiomatic: " The servant did as he was told, and the bandits all let them pass.

sentences.zh: 永安初，就拜南趙郡太守，以好酒，無政績。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan he was appointed on the spot Administrator of Southern Zhao Commandery; because of his love of wine he achieved no administrative merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongan he was appointed on the spot administrator of Southern Zhao Commandery. His love of wine left him no record of merit.

sentences.zh: 值洛陽傾覆，莊帝幽崩，元忠棄官還家，潛圖義舉。

translations.literal: When Luoyang collapsed and Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement, Yuanzhong abandoned his office and returned home, secretly planning a righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell and Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement, Yuanzhong abandoned his office and returned home, secretly planning a righteous rising.

sentences.zh: 會高祖率衆東出，便自往奉迎。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor led his host eastward, he went of his own accord to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan led his host eastward, Yuanzhong went of his own accord to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 乘露車，載素箏濁酒以見高祖，因進從橫之策，備陳誠款，深見嘉納。

translations.literal: He rode an open carriage, bearing a plain zither and unstrained wine to see the Grand Ancestor; he thereupon advanced strategies of alliance and opposition, declaring his loyalty in full, and won deep favor and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: He rode an open carriage, bearing a plain zither and a jar of unstrained wine to see Gao Huan. He thereupon laid out stratagems of alliance and opposition, declared his loyalty in full, and won deep favor.

sentences.zh: 時刺史尒朱羽生阻兵據州，元忠先聚衆於西山，仍與大軍相合，擒斬羽生。

translations.literal: At the time Governor Erzhu Yusheng held the province with rebellious troops; Yuanzhong first gathered a force on Western Mountain, then joined the main army, captured and executed Yusheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Governor Erzhu Yusheng held the province with rebellious troops. Yuanzhong first gathered a force on Western Mountain, then joined the main army, captured Yusheng, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 卽令行殷州事。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered to provisionally administer Yin Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately ordered to provisionally administer Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 中興初，除中軍將軍、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the restoration he was appointed General of the Central Army and Minister Steward.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the restoration he was appointed general of the central army and minister steward.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉太常卿、殷州大中正。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonial and Great Arbiter of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to minister of ceremonial and great arbiter of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 後以從兄瑾年長，以中正讓之。

translations.literal: Later, because his older cousin Jin was senior in years, he yielded the arbiter's post to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his older cousin Jin was senior in years, he yielded the arbiter's post to him.

sentences.zh: 尋加征南將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 武帝將納后，卽高祖之長女也，詔元忠與尚書令元羅致娉於晉陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was about to take an empress — the Grand Ancestor's eldest daughter — he ordered Yuanzhong and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo to conduct the betrothal mission to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojuan was about to take an empress — Gao Huan's eldest daughter — he ordered Yuanzhong and Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo to conduct the betrothal mission to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖每於宴席論敘舊事，因撫掌欣笑云：「此人逼我起兵。

translations.literal: At every feast the Grand Ancestor would recount old affairs, then clap his hands and laugh with delight, saying, "This man drove me to raise the banner.
translations.idiomatic: At every feast Gao Huan would recount old affairs, then clap his hands and laugh with delight. "This man drove me to raise the banner,

sentences.zh: 」賜白馬一匹。

translations.literal: " He was granted one white horse.
translations.idiomatic: " he would say, and grant him one white horse.

sentences.zh: 元忠戲謂高祖曰：「若不與侍中，當更覓建義處。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong joked to the Grand Ancestor, "If you do not make me palace attendant, I shall find another place to raise the banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong joked to Gao Huan, "If you do not make me palace attendant, I shall find another place to raise the banner.

sentences.zh: 」高祖答曰：「建義處不慮無，止畏如此老翁不可遇耳。

translations.literal: " The Grand Ancestor replied, "Places to raise the banner are not lacking — I only fear that an old man like this cannot be encountered again.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan replied, "Places to raise the banner are not lacking — I only fear that an old man like this cannot be encountered again.

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「止為此翁難遇，所以不去。

translations.literal: " Yuanzhong said, "It is precisely because this old man is hard to meet that I do not leave.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanzhong said, "It is precisely because this old man is hard to meet that I do not leave.

sentences.zh: 」因捋高祖鬚而大笑。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he seized the Grand Ancestor's beard and laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he seized Gao Huan's beard and laughed loudly.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦悉其雅意，深相嘉重。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor also fully grasped his refined intent and valued him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan also fully grasped his refined intent and valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 後高祖奉送皇后，仍田於晉澤，元忠馬倒被傷，當時殞絕，久而方蘇。

translations.literal: Later, when the Grand Ancestor escorted the empress and was hunting at Jin Marsh, Yuanzhong's horse fell and injured him; he collapsed on the spot and only revived after a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gao Huan escorted the empress and was hunting at Jin Marsh, Yuanzhong's horse fell and injured him. He collapsed on the spot and only revived after a long time.

sentences.zh: 高祖親自撫視。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor personally tended to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan personally tended to him.

sentences.zh: 其年，封晉陽縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: That year he was enfeoffed Baron of Jinyang County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was enfeoffed baron of Jinyang County with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後以微譴失官。

translations.literal: Later for a minor offense he lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for a minor offense, he lost his office.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷離貳，義旗多見猜阻。

translations.literal: At the time the court was divided, and those of the righteous banner were often suspected and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was divided, and men of the righteous banner were often suspected and obstructed.

sentences.zh: 斛斯椿等以元忠淡於榮利，又不以世事經懷，故不在嫌嫉之地。

translations.literal: Husi Chun and the rest, because Yuanzhong was indifferent to glory and profit and did not concern himself with worldly affairs, did not place him among those they envied and resented.
translations.idiomatic: Husi Chun and the rest, because Yuanzhong was indifferent to glory and profit and did not concern himself with worldly affairs, did not count him among those they envied and resented.

sentences.zh: 尋兼中書令。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天平初，復為太常。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was again made Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was again made minister of ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 後加驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was additionally made general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 四年，除使持節、光州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed bearer of the staff and Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed bearer of the staff and governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 時州境災儉，人皆菜色，元忠表求賑貸，俟秋徵收。

translations.literal: At the time the province was stricken by disaster and famine; the people were gaunt with hunger. Yuanzhong memorialized asking for relief grain, to be recovered through autumn collection.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the province was stricken by disaster and famine; the people were gaunt with hunger. Yuanzhong memorialized asking for relief grain, to be recovered through autumn collection.

sentences.zh: 被報，聽用萬石。

translations.literal: In reply he was permitted ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In reply he was permitted ten thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 元忠以為萬石給人，計一家不過升斗而已，徒有虛名，不救其弊，遂出十五萬石以賑之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong judged that ten thousand shi distributed among the people would amount to no more than a sheng or dou per household — empty reputation that would not relieve their distress — and so released one hundred fifty thousand shi to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong judged that ten thousand shi spread among the people would amount to no more than a sheng or dou per household — empty reputation that would not relieve their distress. He released one hundred fifty thousand shi to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 事訖表陳，朝廷嘉而不責。

translations.literal: When the matter was finished he memorialized the facts; the court praised him and did not charge him.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was finished he memorialized the facts. The court praised him and did not charge him.

sentences.zh: 興和末，拜侍中。

translations.literal: At the end of Xinghe he was appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xinghe he was appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 元忠雖居要任，初不以物務干懷，唯以聲酒自娛，大率常醉，家事大小，了不關心。

translations.literal: Though Yuanzhong held important posts, he never let official business weigh on his mind; he amused himself only with music and wine, was for the most part constantly drunk, and paid no attention at all to domestic affairs great or small.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuanzhong held important posts, he never let official business weigh on his mind. He amused himself only with music and wine, was for the most part constantly drunk, and paid no attention at all to domestic affairs great or small.

sentences.zh: 園庭之內，羅種果藥，親朋尋詣，必留連宴賞。

translations.literal: Within his garden he planted fruit and medicinal herbs in abundance; when kinsmen and friends came to call, he always detained them for feasting and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Within his garden he planted fruit and medicinal herbs in abundance. When kinsmen and friends came to call, he always detained them for feasting and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 每挾彈攜壺，敖遊里閈，遇會飲酌，蕭然自得。

translations.literal: He would carry his slingshot and wine flask and roam through the lanes at leisure; whenever he met company for drinking, he was tranquil and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He would carry his slingshot and wine flask and roam through the lanes at leisure. Whenever he met company for drinking, he was tranquil and at ease.

sentences.zh: 常布言於執事云：「年漸遲暮，志力已衰，久忝名官，以妨賢路。

translations.literal: He often spread word among those in charge, saying, "My years approach twilight, my will and strength have declined; I have long held a distinguished office, blocking the path for the able.
translations.idiomatic: He often spread word among those in charge, saying, "My years approach twilight, my will and strength have declined. I have long held a distinguished office, blocking the path for the able.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷厚恩，未便放棄者，乞在閑冗，以養餘年。

translations.literal: If the court's generous grace will not yet release me, I beg an idle, secondary post in which to spend my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: If the court's generous grace will not yet release me, I beg an idle, secondary post in which to spend my remaining years.

sentences.zh: 」武定元年，除東徐州刺史，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: " In Wuding year one he was appointed Governor of Eastern Xu Province but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " In Wuding year one he was appointed governor of Eastern Xu Province but firmly declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 乃除驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was then made General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made general of agile cavalry and equal in protocol to three imperators.

sentences.zh: 曾貢世宗蒲桃一盤。

translations.literal: Once he presented Shizong with a tray of grapes.
translations.idiomatic: Once he presented Gao Cheng with a tray of grapes.

sentences.zh: 世宗報以百練縑，遺其書曰：「儀同位亞台鉉，識懷貞素，出藩入侍，備經要重。

translations.literal: Shizong replied with one hundred bolts of fine silk and sent him a letter saying, "Your rank as Equal in Protocol stands next to the pillars of state; your mind is steadfast and plain; you have served both in the provinces and at court in posts of weight and consequence.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng replied with one hundred bolts of fine silk and sent him a letter saying, "Your rank as equal in protocol stands next to the pillars of state. Your mind is steadfast and plain. You have served both in the provinces and at court in posts of weight and consequence.

sentences.zh: 而猶家無擔石，室若懸磬，豈輕財重義，奉時愛己故也。

translations.literal: Yet your house holds not a single stone's measure, your rooms are as empty as a suspended bell — surely it is because you hold wealth lightly and honor righteousness, serving the age and cherishing yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your house holds not a single stone's measure, your rooms are as empty as a suspended bell — surely it is because you hold wealth lightly and honor righteousness, serving the age and cherishing yourself.

sentences.zh: 久相嘉尚，嗟詠無極，恒思標賞，有意無由。

translations.literal: I have long admired you, my praise knows no limit; I have always wished to mark my esteem, but found no occasion.
translations.idiomatic: I have long admired you, my praise knows no limit. I have always wished to mark my esteem, but found no occasion.

sentences.zh: 忽辱蒲桃，良深佩帶。

translations.literal: Now your gift of grapes comes as a surprise — I am deeply touched.
translations.idiomatic: Now your gift of grapes comes as a surprise — I am deeply touched.

sentences.zh: 聊用絹百疋，以酬清德也。

translations.literal: I send one hundred bolts of silk in token of your pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I send one hundred bolts of silk in token of your pure virtue.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 孫騰、司馬子如嘗共詣元忠，見其坐樹下，擁被對壺，庭室蕪曠。

translations.literal: Sun Teng and Sima Ziru once went together to visit Yuanzhong; they found him sitting beneath a tree, wrapped in a quilt facing a wine jar, the courtyard overgrown and deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng and Sima Ziru once went together to visit Yuanzhong. They found him sitting beneath a tree, wrapped in a quilt facing a wine jar, the courtyard overgrown and deserted.

sentences.zh: 謂二公曰：「不意今日披藜藿也。

translations.literal: He said to the two lords, "I never thought to find myself spreading coarse greens for guests today.
translations.idiomatic: He said to the two lords, "I never thought to find myself spreading coarse greens for guests today.

sentences.zh: 」因呼妻出，衣不曳地。

translations.literal: " He called his wife out; her clothes did not even reach the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " He called his wife out; her clothes did not even reach the ground.

sentences.zh: 二公相顧嘆息而去，大餉米絹衣服，元忠受而散之。

translations.literal: The two exchanged glances, sighed, and departed; they sent generous gifts of grain, silk, and clothing, which Yuanzhong accepted and distributed.
translations.idiomatic: The two exchanged glances, sighed, and departed. They sent generous gifts of grain, silk, and clothing, which Yuanzhong accepted and distributed.

sentences.zh: 三年，復以本官領衛尉卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he again held his former office concurrently with Minister Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again held his former office concurrently with minister steward.

sentences.zh: 其年卒於位，年六十。

translations.literal: That year he died in office. He was sixty.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in office. He was sixty.

sentences.zh: 詔贈縑布五百疋，使持節、督定冀殷幽四州諸軍事、大將軍、司徒、定州刺史，諡曰敬惠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted five hundred bolts of silk and cloth, bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ji, Yin, and You, grand general, Duke over the Masses, and Governor of Ding Province, with posthumous title Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted five hundred bolts of silk and cloth, bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, Ji, Yin, and You, grand general, duke over the masses, and governor of Ding Province, with the posthumous title Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 初，元忠將仕，夢手執炬火入其父墓，中夜驚起，甚惡之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuanzhong was about to enter office, he dreamed he held a torch and entered his father's tomb; he woke in the middle of the night in alarm and took it as a bad omen.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yuanzhong was about to enter office, he dreamed he held a torch and entered his father's tomb. He woke in the middle of the night in alarm and took it as a bad omen.

sentences.zh: 旦告其受業師，占云：「大吉，此謂光照先人，終致貴達矣。

translations.literal: At dawn he told his teacher, who divined: "Great fortune — this means light shining upon your ancestors; you will in the end reach honor and eminence.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told his teacher, who divined: "Great fortune — this means light shining upon your ancestors. You will in the end reach honor and eminence.

sentences.zh: 」子搔嗣。

translations.literal: " His son Sao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: " His son Sao inherited.

sentences.zh: 搔，字德況，少聰敏，有才藝，音律博弈之屬，多所通解。

translations.literal: Sao, styled Dekuang, was clever and perceptive in youth, talented in the arts; music, board games, and the like — he mastered many.
translations.idiomatic: Sao, styled Dekuang, was clever and perceptive in youth and talented in the arts. Music, board games, and the like — he mastered many.

sentences.zh: 曾采諸聲，別造一器，號曰八絃，時人稱其思理。

translations.literal: He once gathered various tones and separately devised an instrument called the Eight Strings; men of the age praised his inventive mind.
translations.idiomatic: He once gathered various tones and separately devised an instrument called the Eight Strings. Men of the age praised his inventive mind.

sentences.zh: 起家司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: He first entered service as itinerant staff officer in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as itinerant staff officer in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 累遷河內太守，百姓安之。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Administrator of Henei, where the common people found peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through offices to administrator of Henei, where the common people found peace under him.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as secretary in the Ministry of Rites of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as secretary in the ministry of rites of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 天保八年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 元忠族弟密，字希邕，平棘人也。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong's younger clansman Mi, styled Xiyong, was a native of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong's younger clansman Mi, styled Xiyong, came from Pingji.

sentences.zh: 祖伯膺，魏東郡太守，贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Boying was Administrator of Dong Commandery in Wei, posthumously granted Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Boying was administrator of Dong Commandery in Wei, posthumously granted governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 父煥，治書侍御史、河內太守，贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Huan was supervising secretary of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Henei, posthumously granted Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huan was supervising secretary of the masters of writing, administrator of Henei, posthumously granted governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 密少有節操，屬尒朱兆殺逆，乃陰結豪右，與渤海高昂為報復之計。

translations.literal: Mi in youth had integrity of character; when Erzhu Zhao committed regicide, he secretly joined with leading men and with Gao Ang of Bohai to plan vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: Mi in youth had integrity of character. When Erzhu Zhao committed regicide, he secretly joined with leading men and with Gao Ang of Bohai to plan vengeance.

sentences.zh: 屬高祖出山東，密以兵從舉義，遙授幷州刺史，封容城縣侯，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor came out of Shandong, Mi followed the righteous rising with troops; he was remotely appointed Governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed Marquis of Rongcheng County with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan came out of Shandong, Mi followed the righteous rising with troops. He was remotely appointed governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed marquis of Rongcheng County with a fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆至廣阿，高祖令密募殷、定二州兵五千人鎮黃沙、井陘二道。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao reached Guang'a, the Grand Ancestor ordered Mi to recruit five thousand troops from Yin and Ding provinces to garrison the Yellow Sand and Jingxing passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao reached Guang'a, Gao Huan ordered Mi to recruit five thousand troops from Yin and Ding provinces to garrison the Yellow Sand and Jingxing passes.

sentences.zh: 及兆韓陵敗還晉陽，隨軍平兆。

translations.literal: When Zhao was defeated at Hanling and retreated to Jinyang, Mi followed the army to pacify Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was defeated at Hanling and retreated to Jinyang, Mi followed the army to pacify him.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃以薛循義行幷州事，授密建州刺史。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor then had Xue Xunyi provisionally administer Bing Province affairs and appointed Mi Governor of Jian Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then had Xue Xunyi provisionally administer Bing Province and appointed Mi governor of Jian Province.

sentences.zh: 又除襄州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 在州十餘年，甚得安邊之術，威信聞於外境。

translations.literal: For more than ten years in the province he thoroughly mastered the art of securing the borders; his authority and reputation were known beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years in the province he thoroughly mastered the art of securing the borders. His authority and reputation were known beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 高祖頻降手書勞問，並賜口馬。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor repeatedly sent personal letters of comfort and inquiry, and also granted him provisions and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan repeatedly sent personal letters of comfort and inquiry, and also granted him provisions and horses.

sentences.zh: 侯景外叛，誘密執之，授以官爵。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled abroad, he lured Mi into captivity and granted him office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled abroad, he lured Mi into captivity and granted him office and rank.

sentences.zh: 景敗歸朝，朝廷以密從景非元心，不之罪也。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated and Mi returned to court, the court judged that Mi had followed Jing without genuine intent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was defeated and Mi returned to court, the court judged that Mi had followed Jing without genuine intent and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 天保初，以舊功授散騎常侍，復本爵縣侯，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, for past merit he was appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and restored to his original marquisate of the county; he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, for past merit he was appointed regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and restored to his original county marquisate; he died.

sentences.zh: 贈殿中尚書、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Palace Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted palace director of the masters of writing and governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 密性方直，有行檢。

translations.literal: Mi's character was upright and direct, with proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's character was upright and direct, with proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 因母患積年，得名醫治療，不愈，乃精習經方，洞曉針藥，母疾得除。

translations.literal: Because his mother had been ill for years and famous physicians could not cure her, he thoroughly studied classical prescriptions until he mastered acupuncture and medicine, and his mother's illness was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother had been ill for years and famous physicians could not cure her, he thoroughly studied classical prescriptions until he mastered acupuncture and medicine, and his mother's illness was removed.

sentences.zh: 當世皆服其明解，由是亦以醫術知名。

translations.literal: All his contemporaries admired his clear understanding, and he became renowned for his medical skill as well.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries admired his keen understanding, and he won fame as a physician besides.

sentences.zh: 缺魏末行護軍司馬、武邑太守。

translations.literal: Missing: at the end of Wei he served as adjutant to the Defender-in-Chief and as Governor of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: [Text missing.] At the end of Wei he served as adjutant to the defender-in-chief and as governor of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 天保初，司空長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he served as chief clerk to the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 大寧、武平中，清河、廣平二郡守，銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Daning and Wuping he was Administrator of Qinghe and Guangping and held the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daning and Wuping eras he governed Qinghe and Guangping and held the title grand master for splendid happiness with the silver seal.

sentences.zh: 齊亡後卒。

translations.literal: He died after the fall of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He died after Qi fell.

sentences.zh: 子道謙，武平中，侍御史。

translations.literal: His son Daoqian, during Wuping, was Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoqian served as investigating censor during Wuping.

sentences.zh: 道謙弟道貞，南青州司馬，為逆賊邢杲所殺。

translations.literal: Daoqian's younger brother Daozhen was Adjutant of Southern Qing Province and was killed by the rebel Xing Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian's younger brother Daozhen was adjutant of Southern Qing Province and was killed by the rebel Xing Guo.

sentences.zh: 贈北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Northern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted governor of Northern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 元忠宗人愍，字魔憐，形貌魁傑，見異於時。

translations.literal: Min, a clansman of Yuanzhong, styled Molian, was of towering build and striking appearance, unlike any man of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Min, a clansman of Yuanzhong, styled Molian, was a man of towering build and striking mien — unlike anyone else of his day.

sentences.zh: 少有大志，年四十，猶不仕州郡，唯招致姦俠，以為徒侶。

translations.literal: From youth he nursed great ambitions. Even at forty he still would not take office in prefecture or commandery, but gathered rogues and daredevils as his companions.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he nursed great ambitions. Even at forty he would not serve in prefecture or commandery, gathering rogues and daredevils as his companions instead.

sentences.zh: 孝昌之末，天下兵起，愍潛居林慮山，觀候時變。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang, when warfare erupted across the realm, Min withdrew to Mount Linlu and watched for the turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era, as warfare erupted across the realm, Min withdrew to Mount Linlu and watched for the turn of events.

sentences.zh: 賊帥鮮于修禮、毛普賢作亂，詔遣大都督長孫稚討之。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Xianyu Xiuli and Mao Puxian rose in rebellion. An edict dispatched Grand Commander Changsun Zhi to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chiefs Xianyu Xiuli and Mao Puxian rose in rebellion, and an edict dispatched Grand Commander Changsun Zhi to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 稚素聞愍名，召兼帳內統軍。

translations.literal: Zhi had long heard of Min's reputation and summoned him to serve concurrently as commander of the tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had long heard of Min's reputation and summoned him to serve concurrently as commander of the tent guard.

sentences.zh: 軍達呼沱，賊來逆戰，稚軍為賊所敗，愍遂歸家。

translations.literal: When the army reached Hutuo, the rebels came out to give battle. Zhi's army was defeated by the rebels, and Min returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Hutuo, the rebels came out to fight. Zhi's army was routed, and Min returned home.

sentences.zh: 安樂王元鑒為北道大行臺，至鄴，以賊衆盛強，未得前。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan of Anle served as Grand Mobile Office of the Northern Circuit. When he reached Ye, the rebel forces were so strong that he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan of Anle served as grand mobile office of the northern circuit. When he reached Ye, the rebels were so strong that he could not advance.

sentences.zh: 遣使征愍，表授武騎常侍、假節、別將，鎮鄴城東郭。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to summon Min and memorialized the throne to appoint him Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, with provisional staff and separate command, garrisoning the eastern suburb of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to summon Min and memorialized the throne to appoint him cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, with provisional staff and separate command, garrisoning the eastern suburb of Ye.

sentences.zh: 葛榮之圍信都，餘黨南抄，陽平以北，皆為賊有。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong besieged Xindu, his remnant bands raided southward, and all lands north of Yangping fell into rebel hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong besieged Xindu, his remnant bands raided southward until all lands north of Yangping lay in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 鑒命愍為前驅，別討之，頗有斬獲。

translations.literal: Yuan ordered Min to serve as vanguard and separately suppress them; he won considerable heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan ordered Min to serve as vanguard and hunt them down separately; he took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 及鑒謀逆，愍乃詐患暴風，鑒信之，因此得免。

translations.literal: When Yuan plotted rebellion, Min feigned a sudden fit of wind sickness. Yuan believed him and thus Min escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan plotted rebellion, Min feigned a sudden fit of wind sickness. Yuan believed him, and Min escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大都督源子邕屯安陽，大都裴衍屯鄴城，西討鑒。

translations.literal: Not long after, Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong encamped at Anyang and Grand Commander Pei Yan encamped at Ye; together they marched west to attack Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong encamped at Anyang and Grand Commander Pei Yan at Ye; together they marched west against Yuan.

sentences.zh: 愍棄家口奔子邕，仍被徵赴洛，除奉車都尉，持節鎮汁河。

translations.literal: Min abandoned his family and fled to Ziyong, then was summoned to the capital and made Keeper of the Imperial Carriages, with staff of authority garrisoning Zhihe.
translations.idiomatic: Min abandoned his family and fled to Ziyong, then was summoned to the capital and made keeper of the imperial carriages, with staff of authority garrisoning Zhihe.

sentences.zh: 汁河在鄴之西北，重山之中，幷、相二州交境。

translations.literal: Zhihe lay northwest of Ye, in the heart of the mountains, on the border between Bing and Xiang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihe lay northwest of Ye, deep in the mountains, on the border between Bing and Xiang provinces.

sentences.zh: 以葛榮南逼，故用愍鎮之。

translations.literal: Because Ge Rong was pressing south, Min was posted there.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ge Rong was pressing south, Min was posted there.

sentences.zh: 榮遣其叔樂陵王葛萇率精騎一萬擊愍，愍據險拒戰，萇不得前。

translations.literal: Ge Rong sent his uncle, Prince Ge of Leling, with ten thousand elite cavalry to attack Min. Min held the defiles and fought them off; Ge could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong sent his uncle, Prince Ge of Leling, with ten thousand elite cavalry to attack Min. Min held the defiles and fought them off, and Ge could not advance.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮至東關，愍乃見榮。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong reached Dongguan, Min went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong reached Dongguan, Min went to see him.

sentences.zh: 榮欲分賊勢，遣愍別道向襄國，襲賊署廣州刺史田怙軍。

translations.literal: Rong wished to divide the rebel forces and sent Min by a separate route toward Xiangguo to strike the army of Tian Hu, whom the rebels had appointed Provisional Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to divide the rebel forces and sent Min by a separate route toward Xiangguo to strike the army of Tian Hu, whom the rebels had appointed provisional governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 愍未至襄國，已擒葛榮。

translations.literal: Before Min reached Xiangguo, Ge Rong had already been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before Min reached Xiangguo, Ge Rong had already been captured.

sentences.zh: 卽表授愍建忠將軍。

translations.literal: He was immediately memorialized for appointment as General Who Establishes Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately memorialized for appointment as general who establishes loyalty.

sentences.zh: 分廣平易陽、襄國，南趙郡之中丘三縣為易陽郡，以愍為太守。

translations.literal: The three counties of Yiyang, Xiangguo, and Zhongqiu — drawn from Guangping and Southern Zhao commanderies — were joined into Yiyang Commandery, and Min was made its Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The three counties of Yiyang, Xiangguo, and Zhongqiu — taken from Guangping and Southern Zhao commanderies — were joined into Yiyang Commandery, and Min was made its administrator.

sentences.zh: 賜爵襄國侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 永安末，假平北將軍、持節、當郡大都督，遷樂平太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongan he was made acting General Who Pacifies the North, with staff of authority and grand governorship of the commandery, and transferred to Administrator of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongan he was made acting general who pacifies the north, with staff of authority and grand governorship of the commandery, and transferred to administrator of Leping.

sentences.zh: 未之郡，洛京傾覆，愍率所部西保石門山。

translations.literal: Before he reached the commandery, Luoyang fell. Min led his troops west to hold Shimen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the commandery, Luoyang fell. Min led his troops west to hold Shimen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 潛與幽州刺史劉靈助及高昂兄弟、安州刺史盧曹等同契義舉。

translations.literal: Secretly he entered into covenant with Liu Lingzhu, Governor of You Province, the Gao brothers of Ganyu, Lu Cao, Governor of An Province, and others to raise the righteous banner together.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he entered into covenant with Liu Lingzhu, governor of You Province, the Gao brothers of Ganyu, Lu Cao, governor of An Province, and others to raise the righteous banner together.

sentences.zh: 助敗，愍遂入石門。

translations.literal: When Lingzhu was defeated, Min withdrew into Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzhu was defeated, Min withdrew into Shimen.

sentences.zh: 高祖建義，以書招愍，愍奉書，擁衆數千人以赴高祖，高祖親迎之。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause, he wrote to summon Min. Min answered the letter and came with several thousand followers to join Gao Huan, who personally went out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause, he wrote to summon Min. Min answered the letter and came with several thousand followers; Gao Huan personally went out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、征南將軍、都督相州諸軍事、相州刺史，兼尚書西南道行臺、當州都督。

translations.literal: He was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Campaigns South, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Xiang Province, and Governor of Xiang Province, and concurrently Director of the Southwest Circuit Mobile Office and Grand Governor of the Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff of authority, general who campaigns south, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Xiang Province, and governor of Xiang Province, and concurrently director of the southwest circuit mobile office and grand governor of the province.

sentences.zh: 令愍率本衆西還舊鎮，高祖親送之。

translations.literal: Min was ordered to lead his original forces back to his old post; Gao Huan personally saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: Min was ordered to lead his original forces back to his old post, and Gao Huan personally saw him off.

sentences.zh: 愍至鄉，據馬鞍山，依險為壘，徵糧集兵，以為聲勢。

translations.literal: When Min reached his home district, he took Mount Ma'an, built fortifications in the defiles, levied grain, and gathered troops to make a show of strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Min reached his home district, he took Mount Ma'an, built fortifications in the defiles, levied grain, and gathered troops to make a show of strength.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆出井陘，高祖破兆於廣阿。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao came out through Jingxing Pass, and Gao Huan defeated him at Guang'a.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao came out through Jingxing Pass, and Gao Huan defeated him at Guang'a.

sentences.zh: 愍統其本衆，屯故城以備尒朱兆。

translations.literal: Min commanded his original forces and encamped at the old city to guard against Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Min commanded his original forces and encamped at the old city to guard against Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 相州既平，命愍還鄴，除西南道行臺都官尚書，復屯故城。

translations.literal: Once Xiang Province was pacified, Min was ordered back to Ye and made Director of the Masters of Writing for the Southwest Circuit Mobile Office, again encamping at the old city.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiang Province was pacified, Min was ordered back to Ye and made director of the masters of writing for the southwest circuit mobile office, again encamping at the old city.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆等將至，高祖徵愍參守鄴城。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao and the others were about to arrive, Gao Huan summoned Min to help defend Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao and the others were about to arrive, Gao Huan summoned Min to help defend Ye.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，除太府卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was made Director of the Imperial Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was made director of the imperial treasuries.

sentences.zh: 後出為南荊州刺史、當州大都督。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Governor of Southern Jing Province and Grand Governor of the Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went out as governor of Southern Jing Province and grand governor of the province.

sentences.zh: 此州自孝昌以來，舊路斷絕，前後刺史皆從間道始得達州。

translations.literal: Since Xiaochang this province's old routes had been cut off; successive governors had reached it only by hidden paths.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiaochang the province's old routes had been cut off, and successive governors had reached it only by hidden paths.

sentences.zh: 愍勒部曲數千人，徑向懸瓠，從北陽復舊道，且戰且前三百餘里，所經之處，卽立郵亭，蠻左大服。

translations.literal: Min led several thousand followers of his personal guard straight toward Xuanhu, reopened the old route from Beiyang, and fought his way forward more than three hundred li. Wherever he passed he established postal stations, and the barbarian peoples on the left were deeply impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Min led several thousand followers of his personal guard straight toward Xuanhu, reopened the old route from Beiyang, and fought his way forward more than three hundred li. Wherever he passed he established postal stations, and the frontier peoples were deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 梁遣其南司州刺史任思祖、隨郡太守桓和等率馬步三萬，兼發邊蠻，圍逼下溠戍。

translations.literal: Liang sent its Governor of Southern Si Province Ren Sinzu, Administrator of Suixian Huan He, and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, and also mobilized frontier barbarians, to surround and press the garrison at Xiazhao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent its governor of Southern Si Province Ren Sinzu, administrator of Suixian Huan He, and others with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry, and also mobilized frontier barbarians, to surround and press the garrison at Xiazhao.

sentences.zh: 愍躬自討擊，破之。

translations.literal: Min personally led the counterattack and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Min personally led the counterattack and routed them.

sentences.zh: 詔加車騎將軍。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 愍於州內開立陂梁，溉稻千餘頃，公私賴之。

translations.literal: Within the province Min opened dams and channels and irrigated more than a thousand qing of rice fields; public and private interests alike depended on this.
translations.idiomatic: Within the province Min opened dams and channels and irrigated more than a thousand qing of rice fields, to the benefit of public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 轉行東荊州，仍除驃騎將軍、東荊州刺史、當州大都督，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Jing Province and additionally made General Who Conquers on Horseback, Governor of Eastern Jing Province, Grand Governor of the Province, and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Eastern Jing Province and additionally made general who conquers on horseback, governor of Eastern Jing Province, grand governor of the province, and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 天平二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、定殷二州軍事、儀同、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, military affairs of Ding and Yin provinces, Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, military affairs of Ding and Yin provinces, equal in protocol to three imperators, and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 元忠族叔景遺，少雄武有膽力，好結聚亡命，共為劫盜，鄉里每患之。

translations.literal: Jingyi, Yuanzhong's clansman by marriage, was fierce and bold in youth, with great physical courage. He loved gathering fugitives and outlaws to rob and plunder together, and the neighborhood suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi, Yuanzhong's clansman by marriage, was fierce and bold in youth, with great physical courage. He loved gathering fugitives and outlaws for robbery and plunder, and the neighborhood suffered from him.

sentences.zh: 永安末，其兄南鉅鹿太守無為以贓罪為御史糾劾，禁於州獄。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongan, his elder brother Wuwei, Governor of Southern Julu, was impeached by the censorate for corruption and imprisoned in the provincial jail.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongan, his elder brother Wuwei, governor of Southern Julu, was impeached by the censorate for corruption and imprisoned in the provincial jail.

sentences.zh: 景遺率左右十餘騎，詐稱臺使，徑入州城，劫無為而出之。

translations.literal: Jingyi led a dozen or so mounted followers, falsely claiming to be imperial envoys, and burst straight into the provincial city, seizing Wuwei and freeing him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi led a dozen or so mounted followers, falsely claiming to be imperial envoys, and burst straight into the provincial city to seize Wuwei and free him.

sentences.zh: 州軍追討，竟不能制。

translations.literal: The provincial army pursued and attacked but could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial army pursued and attacked but could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 由是以俠聞。

translations.literal: By this he became renowned for chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: By this he became renowned for chivalry.

sentences.zh: 及高祖舉義於信都，景遺赴於軍門。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Jingyi came to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the righteous cause at Xindu, Jingyi came to the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 高祖素聞其名，接之甚厚。

translations.literal: Gao Huan had long heard his name and received him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan had long heard his name and received him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 命與元忠舉兵於西山，仍與大軍俱會，擒刺史尒朱羽生。

translations.literal: He ordered Jingyi together with Yuanzhong to raise troops on the Western Mountains, then join the main army; they captured and executed Governor Erzhu Yusheng.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jingyi together with Yuanzhong to raise troops on the Western Mountains and join the main army; they captured and executed Governor Erzhu Yusheng.

sentences.zh: 以功除龍驤將軍，昌平縣公，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made General of the Dragon Cavalry, Duke of Changping County, with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made general of the dragon cavalry, duke of Changping County, with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆來伐，又力戰有功，除使持節、大都督、左將軍。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao came to attack, he fought vigorously with further merit and was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander, and Left General.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao came to attack, he fought vigorously with further merit and was made bearer of the staff of authority, grand commander, and left general.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，進爵昌平郡公，增邑三百戶，加車騎將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang his rank was advanced to Duke of Changping Commandery with three hundred additional households, and he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang his rank was advanced to duke of Changping Commandery with three hundred additional households, and he was made general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天平初，出為潁州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he went out as Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he went out as governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為前潁川太守元洪威所襲殺。

translations.literal: Not long after, he was ambushed and killed by the former Administrator of Yingchuan, Yuan Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he was ambushed and killed by the former administrator of Yingchuan, Yuan Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、殷滄二州軍事、大將軍、開府、殷州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Palace Attendant, military affairs of Yin and Cang provinces, Grand General, Opener of a Government Office, and Governor of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted palace attendant, military affairs of Yin and Cang provinces, grand general, opener of a government office, and governor of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 子伽林襲。

translations.literal: His son Qialin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qialin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 盧文偉，字休族，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Wenwei, styled Xizu, was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenwei, styled Xizu, came from Zhuo in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 為北州冠族。

translations.literal: His clan ranked among the foremost families of the Northern Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His clan ranked among the foremost families of the northern provinces.

sentences.zh: 父敞，出後伯假。

translations.literal: His father Chang was adopted as heir by his uncle Bo Jia.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chang was adopted as heir by his uncle Bo Jia.

sentences.zh: 文偉少孤，有志尚，頗涉經史，篤於交遊，少為鄉閭所敬。

translations.literal: Wenwei lost his father early but had lofty aspirations. He read widely in the classics and histories, was devoted to friendship, and in youth was respected by the neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei lost his father early but had lofty aspirations. He read widely in the classics and histories, was devoted to friendship, and in youth was respected throughout the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 年三十八，始舉秀才。

translations.literal: At thirty-eight he was first nominated as a Cultivated Talent.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty-eight he was first nominated as a cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 除本州平北府長流參軍，說刺史裴俊按舊跡修督亢陂，溉田萬餘頃，民賴其利，修立之功，多以委文偉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Adjutant of the Pacifier of the North office in his home province and persuaded Governor Pei Jun to restore the Dukang Dam according to old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing of fields to the people's benefit. Most of the construction work was entrusted to Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief adjutant of the pacifier of the north office in his home province and persuaded Governor Pei Jun to restore the Dukang Dam according to old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing of fields to the people's benefit. Most of the construction work was entrusted to Wenwei.

sentences.zh: 文偉既善於營理，兼展私力，家素貧儉，因此致富。

translations.literal: Since Wenwei excelled at management and also contributed private labor, though his family had been poor and frugal, he grew wealthy thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei excelled at management and also contributed private labor; though his family had been poor and frugal, he grew wealthy thereby.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，詔兼尚書郎中，時行臺常景啟留為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era an edict appointed him concurrently as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; Field Marshal Chang Jing requested that he remain as Bureau Director on the mobile office staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era an edict appointed him concurrently as bureau director in the ministry of revenue; Field Marshal Chang Jing requested that he remain as bureau director on the mobile office staff.

sentences.zh: 及北方將亂，文偉積稻穀於范陽城，時經荒儉，多所賑贍，彌為鄉里所歸。

translations.literal: As the North was on the verge of chaos, Wenwei stockpiled grain in Fanyang city. When famine and dearth struck, he distributed relief generously and won ever greater trust from his neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: As the north was on the verge of chaos, Wenwei stockpiled grain in Fanyang city. When famine and dearth struck, he distributed relief generously and won ever greater trust from his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 尋為杜洛周所虜。

translations.literal: He was soon captured by Du Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon captured by Du Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 洛周敗，復入葛榮，榮敗，歸家。

translations.literal: When Luozhou was defeated he joined Ge Rong; when Rong was defeated he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Luozhou was defeated he joined Ge Rong; when Rong was defeated he returned home.

sentences.zh: 時韓樓據薊城，文偉率鄉閭屯守范陽，與樓相抗。

translations.literal: At that time Han Lou held Jicheng. Wenwei led the neighborhood to hold Fanyang and resist Lou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han Lou held Jicheng. Wenwei led the neighborhood to hold Fanyang and resist Lou.

sentences.zh: 乃以文偉行范陽郡事。

translations.literal: He was then made acting Governor of Fanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made acting governor of Fanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 防守二年，與士卒同勞苦，分散家財，拯救貧乏，莫不人人感說。

translations.literal: For two years he defended the city, sharing hardship with the soldiers, dispersing his family wealth to rescue the destitute; everyone was moved with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: For two years he defended the city, sharing hardship with the soldiers and dispersing his family wealth to rescue the destitute; everyone was moved with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮遣將侯深討樓，平之，文偉以功封大夏縣男，邑二百戶，除范陽太守。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong sent General Hou Shen to suppress Lou. When Lou was pacified, Wenwei was enfeoffed as Baron of Daxia with two hundred households and made Governor of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong sent General Hou Shen to suppress Lou. When Lou was pacified, Wenwei was enfeoffed as baron of Daxia with two hundred households and made governor of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 深乃留鎮范陽。

translations.literal: Hou Shen remained to garrison Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Shen remained to garrison Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 及榮誅，文偉知深難信，乃誘之出獵，閉門拒之。

translations.literal: After Rong was executed, Wenwei knew Shen could not be trusted. He lured him out on a hunt and shut the gates against him.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong was executed, Wenwei knew Shen could not be trusted. He lured him out on a hunt and shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 深失據，遂赴中山。

translations.literal: Shen lost his footing and fled to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen lost his footing and fled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 莊帝崩，文偉與幽州刺史劉靈助同謀起義。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang died, Wenwei plotted an uprising together with Liu Lingzhu, Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang died, Wenwei plotted an uprising together with Liu Lingzhu, governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 靈助克瀛州，留文偉行事，自率兵赴定州，為尒朱榮將侯深所敗，文偉棄州，走還本郡，仍與高幹邕兄弟共相影響。

translations.literal: Lingzhu captured Ying Province and left Wenwei to handle affairs while he personally led troops toward Ding Province, but was defeated by Hou Shen, a general of Erzhu Rong. Wenwei abandoned the province and fled back to his home commandery, still acting in concert with the Gao brothers of Ganyu.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhu captured Ying Province and left Wenwei to handle affairs while he personally led troops toward Ding Province, but was defeated by Hou Shen, a general of Erzhu Rong. Wenwei abandoned the province and fled back to his home commandery, still acting in concert with the Gao brothers of Ganyu.

sentences.zh: 屬高祖至信都，文偉遣子懷道奉啟陳誠，高祖嘉納之。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with a memorial expressing loyalty; Gao Huan welcomed this favorably.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with a memorial expressing loyalty, and Gao Huan welcomed it favorably.

sentences.zh: 中興初，除安東將軍、安州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made general who pacifies the east and governor of An Province.

sentences.zh: 時安州未賓，仍居帥任，行幽州事，加鎮軍、正刺史。

translations.literal: An Province had not yet submitted, so he remained in the commander's role, handling affairs of You Province, with additional titles as Suppressing-Army General and regular Governor.
translations.idiomatic: An Province had not yet submitted, so he remained in the commander's role, handling affairs of You Province, with additional titles as suppressing-army general and regular governor.

sentences.zh: 時安州剌史盧曹亦從靈助舉兵，助敗，因據幽州降尒朱兆，兆仍以為刺史，據城不下。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Cao, Governor of An Province, had also raised troops with Lingzhu. When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao seized You Province and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao, who reappointed him governor; Cao held the city and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lu Cao, governor of An Province, had also raised troops with Lingzhu. When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao seized You Province and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao, who reappointed him governor; Cao held the city and would not submit.

sentences.zh: 文偉不得入州，卽於郡所為州治。

translations.literal: Wenwei could not enter the province and established the provincial seat at the commandery capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei could not enter the province and established the provincial seat at the commandery capital.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，遷安州刺史，累加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was transferred to Governor of An Province and cumulatively promoted to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was transferred to governor of An Province and cumulatively promoted to regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 天平末，高祖以文偉行東雍州事，轉行青州事。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping, Gao Huan had Wenwei act for Eastern Yong Province, then transferred him to act for Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianping, Gao Huan had Wenwei act for Eastern Yong Province, then transferred him to act for Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 文偉性輕財，愛賓客，善於撫接，好行小惠，是以所在頗得人情，雖有受納，吏民不甚苦之。

translations.literal: Wenwei was light with wealth, loved entertaining guests, skilled at winning people over, and fond of small favors; therefore he won considerable goodwill wherever he served. Though he accepted bribes, officials and commoners did not greatly suffer from it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei was light with wealth, loved entertaining guests, skilled at winning people over, and fond of small favors; therefore he won considerable goodwill wherever he served. Though he accepted bribes, officials and commoners did not greatly suffer from it.

sentences.zh: 經紀生資，常若不足，致財積聚，承候寵要，餉遺不絕。

translations.literal: In managing his livelihood he often seemed to lack enough, yet he amassed wealth, currying favor with the powerful and sending gifts without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In managing his livelihood he often seemed to lack enough, yet he amassed wealth, currying favor with the powerful and sending gifts without cease.

sentences.zh: 興和三年卒於州，年六十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe he died in office at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xinghe he died in office at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、都督定瀛殷三州軍事、司徒、尚書左僕射、定州刺史，諡曰孝威。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, Grand Tutor, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ding Province; posthumous title Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Ding, Ying, and Yin provinces, grand tutor, left vice director of the masters of writing, and governor of Ding Province, with the posthumous title Xiaowei.

sentences.zh: 子恭道，性溫良，頗有文學。

translations.literal: His son Gongdao was mild and good-natured by temperament and possessed considerable literary accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongdao was gentle by nature and well versed in letters.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 李崇北征，以為開府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Li Chong marched north on campaign, he was appointed ink-and-record staff officer of an opened government office.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong marched north on campaign, Gongdao was made ink-and-record staff officer to his opened government office.

sentences.zh: 自文偉據范陽，屢經寇難，恭道常助父防守。

translations.literal: From the time Wenwei held Fanyang, through repeated invasions and calamities, Gongdao often helped his father in defense.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Lu Wenwei held Fanyang, through raid after raid, Gongdao often stood at his father's side in defense.

sentences.zh: 七兵尚書郭秀素與恭道交款，及任事，每稱薦之，高祖亦聞其名。

translations.literal: Guo Xiu, minister of the seven armories, had long been on intimate terms with Gongdao; once he took office, he repeatedly praised and recommended him, and the Grand Ancestor also heard his name.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu, minister of the seven armories, had long been close to Gongdao; once in power, he spoke of him again and again, and Gao Huan came to know the name.

sentences.zh: 天平初，特除龍驤將軍、范陽太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was specially appointed flying-cavalry general and governor of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was specially appointed flying-cavalry general and governor of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 在郡有德惠。

translations.literal: In the commandery he showed virtue and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he governed with virtue and kindness.

sentences.zh: 先文偉卒。

translations.literal: He died before Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: He died before his father Wenwei.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、都督幽平二州軍事、幽州刺史、度支尚書，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs in You and Ping provinces, governor of You Province, and minister of revenue; posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, supervision of military affairs in You and Ping provinces, governorship of You Province, and the ministry of revenue; posthumous title Ding, "Settled."

sentences.zh: 子詢祖，襲祖爵大夏男。

translations.literal: His son Xunzu inherited his grandfather's title, Baron of Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xunzu inherited his grandfather's title, baron of Daxia.

sentences.zh: 有術學，文章華靡，為後生之俊。

translations.literal: He had expertise in arts and learning; his writings were florid and ornate — a brilliant man among the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in the arts and sciences, he wrote in a florid, ornate style, and stood among the finest of the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才入京。

translations.literal: Recommended as a provincial graduate, he entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a provincial graduate, he went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 李祖勳嘗宴文士，顯祖使小黃門勑祖勳曰：「茹茹既破，何故無賀表？

translations.literal: Li Zuxun once held a banquet for men of letters; Emperor Xianzu sent a palace attendant eunuch to instruct Zuxun: "The Rouran have been destroyed — why is there no congratulatory memorial?
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuxun once gathered men of letters for a feast; Gao Yang sent a palace attendant with an order for Zuxun: "The Rouran are broken — where is your congratulatory memorial?

sentences.zh: 」使者佇立待之。

translations.literal: The messenger stood waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger stood waiting.

sentences.zh: 諸賓皆為表，詢祖俄頃便成。

translations.literal: All the guests drafted memorials; Xunzu finished his in no time.
translations.idiomatic: Every guest set to drafting a memorial; Xunzu finished his in moments.

sentences.zh: 後朝廷大遷除，同日催拜。

translations.literal: Later the court made mass appointments and promotions, summoning men to take office on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court issued a wave of appointments, summoning men to take office all on the same day.

sentences.zh: 詢祖立於東止車門外，為二十餘人作表，文不加點，辭理可觀。

translations.literal: Xunzu stood outside the East Gate Where Chariots Stop and drafted memorials for more than twenty men — his text needed no correction, and the language and reasoning were admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzu stood outside the East Gate Where Chariots Stop and drafted memorials for more than twenty men — not a word to revise, the language clear and the reasoning sound.

sentences.zh: 詢祖初襲爵封大夏男，有宿德朝士謂之曰：「大夏初成。

translations.literal: When Xunzu first inherited the title and was enfeoffed Baron of Daxia, an elder statesman of long standing said to him: "Great Summer is just forming."
translations.idiomatic: When Xunzu first inherited his title as baron of Daxia, an elder statesman of long standing said to him: "Great Summer is just taking shape."

sentences.zh: 」應聲答曰：「且得燕雀相賀。

translations.literal: He answered on the spot: "For now let the sparrows and swallows congratulate one another."
translations.idiomatic: He answered at once: "For now let sparrow and swallow congratulate each other."

sentences.zh: 」天保末，以職出為築長城子使。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, because of his office he was sent out as sub-official in charge of building the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao, by virtue of his office he was sent out as sub-official in charge of building the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 自負其才，內懷鬱怏，遂毀容服如賤役者，以見楊愔。

translations.literal: Proud of his talent and inwardly resentful, he disheveled his appearance and dressed like a menial laborer to see Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his gifts and smoldering inside, he disheveled his dress and appeared like a common laborer when he went to see Yang Yin.

sentences.zh: 愔曰：「故舊皆有所縻，唯大夏未加處分。

translations.literal: Yin said: "Old friends have all been given posts — only Great Summer has received no appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin said: "Every old friend has been given a post — only Great Summer has not."

sentences.zh: 」詢祖厲聲曰：「是誰之咎！

translations.literal: Xunzu said in a harsh voice: "Whose fault is that!"
translations.idiomatic: Xunzu cried out: "Whose fault is that!"

sentences.zh: 」既至役所，作《築長城賦》，其略曰：「板則紫柏，杵則木瓜，何斯材而斯用也？

translations.literal: Once he reached his posting, he composed "Rhapsody on Building the Long Wall," which in part reads: "Planks of purple cypress, pestles of papaya — what sort of timber for what sort of use?"
translations.idiomatic: Once at his posting he wrote "Rhapsody on Building the Long Wall," which in part reads: "Planks of purple cypress, pestles of papaya — what timber for what task?"

sentences.zh: 草則離離靡靡，緣崗而殖，但使十步而有一芳，余亦何辭間於荊棘。

translations.literal: "Grass grows lush and tangled, clinging to the hillsides; if only every ten paces there were a fragrant bloom, I would have no quarrel with dwelling among thorns."
translations.idiomatic: "Grass grows lush and tangled along the hills — if only every ten paces held a fragrant bloom, I would have no complaint about dwelling among thorns."

sentences.zh: 」邢邵曾戲曰：「卿少年才學富盛，戴角者無上齒，恐卿不壽。

translations.literal: Xing Shao once joked: "You are young and your talent and learning abundant — horned beasts have no upper teeth; I fear you will not live long."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao once teased him: "You are young and your talent runs deep — but horned beasts have no upper teeth; I fear you will not live long."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「詢祖初聞此言，實懷恐懼，見丈人蒼蒼在鬢，差以自安。

translations.literal: He replied: "When Xunzu first heard these words, I truly felt fear — but seeing you, elder, with gray hair at your temples, I am somewhat reassured."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "When I first heard that, I was genuinely afraid — but seeing your temples gone gray, elder, I take some comfort."

sentences.zh: 」邵甚重其敏贍。

translations.literal: Shao greatly valued his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: Shao greatly admired his quick wit.

sentences.zh: 既有口辯，好臧否人物，嘗語人曰：「我昨東方未明，過和氏門外，已見二陸兩源，森然與槐柳齊列。

translations.literal: Endowed with eloquence, he loved to praise and blame others; he once told someone: "Yesterday, before dawn, passing outside the He family gate, I already saw two Lus and two Yuans, standing tall alongside the locust trees and willows."
translations.idiomatic: Gifted with a sharp tongue, he loved to pass judgment on others; he once told someone: "Yesterday, before dawn, I passed the He family gate and already saw two Lus and two Yuans standing tall as locust and willow."

sentences.zh: 」蓋謂彥師、仁惠與文宗、那延也，邢邵盛譽盧思道，以詢祖為不及。

translations.literal: He meant Yan Shi and Renhui, and Wenzong and Nayan; Xing Shao lavishly praised Lu Sidao and held that Xunzu fell short.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Lu Yan Shi and Lu Renhui, and Yuan Wenzong and Yuan Nayan; Xing Shao lavishly praised Lu Sidao and judged Xunzu the lesser man.

sentences.zh: 詢祖曰：「見未能高飛者借其羽毛，知逸勢沖天者剪其翅翮。

translations.literal: Xunzu said: "Those who see one unable to soar high borrow him their feathers; those who know one whose momentum would pierce the sky clip his wings."
translations.idiomatic: Xunzu said: "Those who see a man who cannot yet soar lend him their feathers; those who know a man whose momentum would pierce the sky clip his wings."

sentences.zh: 」謗毀日至，素論皆薄其為人。

translations.literal: Slander reached him day by day, and public opinion generally held his character in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Slander reached him day by day, and public opinion turned against his character.

sentences.zh: 長廣太守邢子廣目二盧云：「詢祖有規檢禰衡，思道無冰棱文舉。

translations.literal: Xing Ziguang, governor of Changguang, sized up the two Lus and said: "Xunzu has the self-restraint of Mi Heng; Sidao lacks the icy edge of Kong Rong."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Ziguang, governor of Changguang, sized up the two Lus and said: "Xunzu has the self-restraint of Mi Heng; Sidao lacks the icy edge of Kong Rong."

sentences.zh: 」後頗折節。

translations.literal: Later he somewhat restrained his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Later he somewhat restrained his conduct.

sentences.zh: 歷太子舍人、司徒記室，卒官。

translations.literal: He served as aide to the heir apparent and recorder of the chancellor's office, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide to the heir apparent and recorder of the chancellor's office, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，皆致遺逸。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in ten scrolls, all now lost.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected writings in ten scrolls, all now lost.

sentences.zh: 嘗為趙郡王妃鄭氏制挽歌詞，其一篇云：「君王盛海內，伉儷盡寰中。

translations.literal: He once composed dirge lyrics for Princess of Zhao Commandery, Lady Zheng, of which one piece reads: "The sovereign's dominion fills the seas; consorts and pairs fill the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed dirge lyrics for Princess of Zhao Commandery, Lady Zheng; one piece reads: "The sovereign's dominion fills the seas; consorts and pairs fill the realm.

sentences.zh: 女儀掩鄭國，嬪容映趙宮。

translations.literal: A woman's propriety eclipses the state of Zheng; a consort's grace outshines the palace of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's propriety eclipses the state of Zheng; a consort's grace outshines the palace of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 春艷桃花水，秋度桂枝風。

translations.literal: Spring dyes the peach-blossom waters; autumn rides the cassia-branch winds.
translations.idiomatic: Spring dyes the peach-blossom waters; autumn rides the cassia-branch winds.

sentences.zh: 遂使叢臺夜，明月滿床空。」

translations.literal: And so on the night at the Cluster Terrace, bright moon filled the empty bed."
translations.idiomatic: And so on the night at the Cluster Terrace, bright moon filled the empty bed."

sentences.zh: 恭道弟懷道，性輕率好酒，頗有慕尚，以守范陽勳，出身員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Gongdao's younger brother Huaidao was light and impulsive, fond of wine, and possessed considerable ambition; for merit in holding Fanyang he entered service as supernumerary attendant cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Gongdao's younger brother Huaidao was light and impulsive, fond of wine, and ambitious; for merit in holding Fanyang he entered service as supernumerary attendant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 文偉遣奉啟詣高祖。

translations.literal: Wenwei dispatched him to deliver a memorial to the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenwei dispatched him to deliver a memorial to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 中興初，加平西將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made general who pacifies the west and grand master of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was additionally made general who pacifies the west and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 元象初，行臺薛琡表行平州事，勳赴霸府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the mobile headquarters submitted a memorial appointing him acting administrator of Ping Province affairs; for merit he went to the Overlord's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the mobile headquarters submitted a memorial appointing him acting administrator of Ping Province affairs; for merit he went to the overlord's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 興和中，行汾州事。

translations.literal: During Xinghe he administered Fen Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Xinghe he administered Fen Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 懷道家預義舉，高祖親待之，出為烏蘇鎮城都督，卒官。

translations.literal: Huaidao's family had joined in raising the righteous banner; the Grand Ancestor treated him with personal favor and sent him out as garrison commander of Wusu, where he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidao's family had joined in raising the righteous banner; Gao Huan treated him with personal favor and sent him out as garrison commander of Wusu, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 懷道弟宗道，性粗率，重任俠。

translations.literal: Huaidao's younger brother Zongdao was coarse and impulsive by nature, and heavily valued chivalric loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidao's younger brother Zongdao was coarse and impulsive by nature, and heavily valued chivalric loyalty.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎、通直散騎常侍，後行南營州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as master of writing and attendant at court with regular attendance, and later acted as governor of Southern Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as master of writing and attendant at court with regular attendance, and later acted as governor of Southern Ying Province.
