sentences.zh: 嘗於晉陽置酒，賓遊滿坐。

translations.literal: He once set out wine at Jinyang; guests and companions filled the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He once set out wine at Jinyang; guests and companions filled the hall.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人馬士達目其彈箜篌女妓云：「手甚纖素。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Attendant Ma Shida eyed his female konghou player and said: "Her hands are very slender and fair."
translations.idiomatic: Palace secretariat attendant Ma Shida eyed his female konghou player and said: "Her hands are very slender and fair."

sentences.zh: 」宗道卽以此婢遺士達，士達固辭，宗道便命家人將解其腕，士達不得已而受之。

translations.literal: Zongdao immediately gave this maid to Shida; Shida firmly declined, so Zongdao ordered his household to cut off her wrist — Shida had no choice but to accept her.
translations.idiomatic: Zongdao immediately gave the maid to Shida; Shida firmly declined, so Zongdao ordered his household to cut off her wrist — Shida had no choice but to accept her.

sentences.zh: 將赴營州，於督亢陂大集鄉人，殺牛聚會。

translations.literal: About to depart for Ying Province, he gathered the district folk at the Dukang Dam, slaughtered cattle, and held a great feast.
translations.idiomatic: About to depart for Ying Province, he gathered the district folk at the Dukang Dam, slaughtered cattle, and held a great feast.

sentences.zh: 有一舊門生酒醉，言辭之間，微有疏失，宗道遂令沉之於水。

translations.literal: An old student, drunk, let slip some improper words in conversation; Zongdao thereupon ordered him drowned in the water.
translations.idiomatic: An old student, drunk, let slip some improper words; Zongdao thereupon ordered him drowned.

sentences.zh: 後坐酷濫除名。

translations.literal: Later, for cruelty and excess he was dismissed and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for cruelty and excess he was dismissed and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 文偉族人勇，字季禮，父璧，魏下邳太守。

translations.literal: Wenwei's clansman Yong, styled Jili, had a father Bi who was governor of Xiapi in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenwei's clansman Yong, styled Jili, had a father Bi who was governor of Xiapi in Wei.

sentences.zh: 勇初從兄景裕俱在學，其叔同稱之曰：「白頭必以文通，季禮當以武達，興吾門在二子也。

translations.literal: In youth Yong and his elder cousin Jingyu were both in school; their uncle Tong praised them: "The white-haired one will surely excel in letters; Jili will surely reach distinction in arms — the raising of our house rests on these two."
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yong and his elder cousin Jingyu were both in school; their uncle Tong praised them: "The white-haired one will surely excel in letters; Jili will surely reach distinction in arms — the raising of our house rests on these two."

sentences.zh: 」幽州反者僕骨那以勇為本郡范陽王，時年十八。

translations.literal: Pugu Na, rebel of You Province, made Yong prince of Fanyang in his native commandery when Yong was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Na, rebel of You Province, made Yong prince of Fanyang in his native commandery when Yong was eighteen.

sentences.zh: 後葛榮作亂，又以勇為燕王。

translations.literal: Later, when Ge Rong raised disorder, Yong was again made Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ge Rong raised disorder, Yong was again made Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 義旗之起也，盧文偉召之，不應。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, Lu Wenwei summoned him, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner was raised, Lu Wenwei summoned him, but he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 尒朱滅後，乃赴晉陽。

translations.literal: Only after the Erzhu were destroyed did he go to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Erzhu were destroyed did he go to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖署勇丞相主簿。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor appointed Yong chief clerk to the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan appointed Yong chief clerk to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 屬山西霜儉，運山東鄉租輸，皆令載實，違者治罪，令勇典其事。

translations.literal: At that time the west of the mountains suffered frost and famine; rent grain from the east was transported in — all were ordered to load full measure, with punishment for violators; Yong was put in charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the west of the mountains suffered frost and famine; rent grain from the east was transported in — all were ordered to load full measure, with punishment for violators; Yong was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 瑯邪公主虛僦千餘車，勇繩劾之。

translations.literal: The Princess of Langye falsely claimed more than a thousand carts; Yong impeached her.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Langye falsely claimed more than a thousand carts; Yong impeached her.

sentences.zh: 公主訴於高祖，而勇守法不屈。

translations.literal: The princess appealed to the Grand Ancestor, but Yong upheld the law and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The princess appealed to Gao Huan, but Yong upheld the law and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂郭秀曰：「盧勇懍懍有不可犯之色，真公直人也，方當委之大事，豈直納租而已。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor told Guo Xiu: "Lu Yong has an unyielding, inviolable bearing — a truly upright man; he should be entrusted with great affairs, not merely collecting rent."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan told Guo Xiu: "Lu Yong has an unyielding, inviolable bearing — a truly upright man; he should be entrusted with great affairs, not merely collecting rent."

sentences.zh: 」遷汝北太守，行陜州事，轉行洛州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Rubei, administered Shaan Province affairs, and then administered Luo Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Rubei, administered Shaan Province affairs, and then administered Luo Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 元象元年，官軍圍廣州，數旬未拔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang, the imperial army besieged Guangzhou for several tens of days without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxiang, the imperial army besieged Guangzhou for several tens of days without taking it.

sentences.zh: 行臺侯景聞西魏救兵將至，集諸將議之。

translations.literal: Mobile headquarters commander Hou Jing, hearing that Western Wei relief troops were about to arrive, gathered the generals to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile headquarters commander Hou Jing, hearing that Western Wei relief troops were about to arrive, gathered the generals to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 勇進觀形勢，於是率百騎，各籠一匹馬。

translations.literal: Yong went forward to observe the situation; thereupon he led a hundred horsemen, each covering one horse with a cage.
translations.idiomatic: Yong went forward to observe the situation; thereupon he led a hundred horsemen, each covering one horse with a cage.

sentences.zh: 至大隗山，知魏將李景和率軍將至。

translations.literal: Reaching Mount Dawei, he learned that Wei general Li Jinghe was leading an army and would soon arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Mount Dawei, he learned that Wei general Li Jinghe was leading an army and would soon arrive.

sentences.zh: 勇多置幡旗於樹頭，分騎為十隊，鳴角直前，擒西魏儀同程華，斬儀同王征蠻，驅馬三百匹，通夜而還。

translations.literal: Yong planted many banners and flags in the treetops, divided his cavalry into ten squads, sounded horns and charged straight ahead, captured Western Wei acting third-grade-equal Li Chenghua, beheaded acting third-grade-equal Wang Zhengman, drove off three hundred horses, and returned through the night.
translations.idiomatic: Yong planted many banners and flags in the treetops, divided his cavalry into ten squads, sounded horns and charged straight ahead, captured Western Wei acting third-grade-equal Li Chenghua, beheaded acting third-grade-equal Wang Zhengman, drove off three hundred horses, and returned through the night.

sentences.zh: 廣州守將駱超以城降，高祖令勇行廣州事。

translations.literal: Guangzhou's defending commander Luo Chao surrendered the city; the Grand Ancestor appointed Yong to administer Guangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou's defending commander Luo Chao surrendered the city; Gao Huan appointed Yong to administer Guangzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 以功授儀同三司、陽州刺史，鎮宜陽。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted acting third-grade-equal, governor of Yang Province, and garrisoned at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was granted acting third-grade-equal, governor of Yang Province, and garrisoned at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 叛民韓木蘭、陳忻等常為邊患，勇大破之。

translations.literal: Rebel commoners Han Mulan, Chen Xin, and others were constant border troubles; Yong routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel commoners Han Mulan, Chen Xin, and others were constant border troubles; Yong routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 啟求入朝，高祖賜勇書曰：「吾委卿陽州，唯安枕高臥，無西南之慮矣。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting to enter court; the Grand Ancestor sent Yong a letter: "I have entrusted Yang Province to you — you need only sleep with pillow high and lie at ease, with no worries from the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting to enter court; Gao Huan sent Yong a letter: "I have entrusted Yang Province to you — you need only sleep with pillow high and lie at ease, with no worries from the southwest.

sentences.zh: 但依朝廷所委，表啟宜停。

translations.literal: But as the court has entrusted you, memorials and reports should cease.
translations.idiomatic: But as the court has entrusted you, memorials and reports should cease.

sentences.zh: 卿之妻子任在州住，當使漢兒之中無在卿前者。

translations.literal: Your wife and children may remain in the province; among the Han children there shall be none who rank above you."
translations.idiomatic: Your wife and children may remain in the province; among the Han children there shall be none who rank above you."

sentences.zh: 」武定二年卒，年三十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding he died, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he died, aged thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 勇有馬五百匹，繕造甲仗六車，遺啟盡獻之朝廷。

translations.literal: Yong had five hundred horses and six carts of armor and weapons freshly made; in his final memorial he presented them all to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had five hundred horses and six carts of armor and weapons freshly made; in his final memorial he presented them all to the court.

sentences.zh: 賻物之外，別賜布絹四千疋。

translations.literal: Beyond the funeral gifts, he was separately granted four thousand bolts of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the funeral gifts, he was separately granted four thousand bolts of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、冀州刺史，諡曰武貞侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted minister of works, governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Marquis Wuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted minister of works and governor of Ji Province; posthumous title Marquis Wuzhen.

sentences.zh: 李義深，趙郡高邑人也。

translations.literal: Li Yishen was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yishen was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖真，魏中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was attendant master of writing in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen was attendant master of writing in Wei.

sentences.zh: 父紹宗，殷州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Shaozong was administrative aide of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaozong was administrative aide of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 義深學涉經史，有當世才用。

translations.literal: Yishen's learning ranged across the classics and histories; he possessed talent useful to his age.
translations.idiomatic: Yishen's learning ranged across the classics and histories; he possessed talent useful to his age.

sentences.zh: 解褐濟州征東府功曹參軍，累加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He began office as merit officer of the eastern campaign staff of Ji Province and was repeatedly promoted to flying-cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: He began office as merit officer of the eastern campaign staff of Ji Province and was repeatedly promoted to flying-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 義旗初，歸高祖於信都，以為大行臺郎中。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was first raised, he joined the Grand Ancestor at Xindu and was made master of writing of the great mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner was first raised, he joined Gao Huan at Xindu and was made master of writing of the great mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 中興初，除平南將軍、鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the south and vice minister of the court of imperial entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was appointed general who pacifies the south and vice minister of the court of imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 義深見尒朱兆兵盛，遂叛高祖奔之。

translations.literal: Yishen saw that Erzhu Zhao's troops were strong and thereupon rebelled against the Grand Ancestor and fled to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Yishen saw that Erzhu Zhao's troops were strong and thereupon rebelled against Gao Huan and fled to join him.

sentences.zh: 兆平，高祖恕其罪，以為大丞相府記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Zhao was pacified, the Grand Ancestor pardoned his crime and made him recorder of the great chancellor's government office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was pacified, Gao Huan pardoned his crime and made him recorder of the great chancellor's government office.

sentences.zh: 累遷左光祿大夫、相府司馬，所經稱職。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left grand master of splendid happiness and chancellor's marshal; in every post he was praised as competent.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to left grand master of splendid happiness and chancellor's marshal; in every post he was praised as competent.

sentences.zh: 轉幷州長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief administrator of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 時刺史可朱渾道元不親細務，民事多委義深，甚濟機速。

translations.literal: At that time Governor Kezhun Hun Daoyuan did not attend to minor affairs; civil matters were largely entrusted to Yishen, who handled them with great dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Governor Kezhun Hun Daoyuan did not attend to minor affairs; civil matters were largely entrusted to Yishen, who handled them with great dispatch.

sentences.zh: 復為大丞相司馬。

translations.literal: He again served as the great chancellor's marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as the great chancellor's marshal.

sentences.zh: 武定中，除齊州剌史，好財利，多所受納。

translations.literal: During Wuding he was appointed governor of Qi Province; he was fond of wealth and profit and accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuding he was appointed governor of Qi Province; he was fond of wealth and profit and accepted many bribes.

sentences.zh: 天保初，行鄭州事，轉行梁州事，尋除散騎常侍，為陽夏太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he administered Zheng Province affairs, then administered Liang Province affairs; soon he was appointed attendant cavalry with regular attendance and made governor of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he administered Zheng Province affairs, then administered Liang Province affairs; soon he was appointed attendant cavalry with regular attendance and made governor of Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 段業告其在州聚斂，被禁止，送梁州窮治，未竟。

translations.literal: Duan Ye reported that he had amassed wealth in the province; he was placed under arrest, sent to Liang Province for thorough investigation, and the case was not yet concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ye reported that he had amassed wealth in the province; he was placed under arrest, sent to Liang Province for thorough investigation, and the case was not yet concluded.

sentences.zh: 三年，遇疾，卒於禁所，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the third year he fell ill and died in confinement, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he fell ill and died in confinement, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子騊駼，有才辯，尚書郎、鄴縣令，武平初，兼通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Taotao was talented and eloquent; he served as master of writing and magistrate of Ye County, and at the beginning of Wuping concurrently held attendant at court with regular attendance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taotao was talented and eloquent; he served as master of writing and magistrate of Ye County, and at the beginning of Wuping concurrently held attendant at court with regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 聘陳，為陳人所稱。

translations.literal: Sent on a mission to Chen, he was praised by the men of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on a mission to Chen, he was praised by the men of Chen.

sentences.zh: 後為壽陽道行臺左丞，與王琳等同陷。

translations.literal: Later he served as Left Assistant Director of the Shouyang Route Office and was captured together with Wang Lin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became left assistant director on the Shouyang route staff and was taken prisoner along with Wang Lin and his companions.

sentences.zh: 周末逃歸。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhou dynasty he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou dynasty drew to its close, he broke free and made his way home.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，永安太守。

translations.literal: In the early Kaihuang era he was Administrator of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang reign he served as prefect of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 卒於絳州長史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Chief Administrator of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as chief administrator of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 子正藻，明敏有才幹。

translations.literal: His son Zhengzao was bright, quick-witted, and capable.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengzao was quick-minded and gifted with real capacity.

sentences.zh: 武平末，儀同開府行參軍、判集書省事。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was a Palace Corps military attendant with honorary general's retinue rank, adjudicating Secretarial Archive affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Wuping he held the rank of palace-corps military attendant with an opening-establishment commission and supervised the secretarial archive.

sentences.zh: 以父騊駼沒陳，正藻便謝病解職，憂思毀瘠，居處飲食若在喪之禮，人士稱之。

translations.literal: Because his father Taotuo had died in Chen captivity, Zhengzao immediately pleaded illness and resigned his office; grief wore him to the bone, and in dwelling, conduct, and meals he kept to the rites of mourning — men of worth praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Taotuo perished in Chen captivity, Zhengzao at once pleaded illness and quit his post. Grief wore him thin; in how he lived, moved, and ate he kept to mourning rites as though the coffin still stood in the hall — and men of judgment praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，歷尚書工部員外郎、盩厔縣令。

translations.literal: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he served in succession as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works within the Masters of Writing and as magistrate of Zhouzhi County.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, during Kaihuang, he served in turn as outer gentleman in the works bureau of the masters of writing and as magistrate of Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 卒於宜州長史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Chief Administrator of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as chief administrator of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 騊駼弟文師，中書舍人、齊郡太守。

translations.literal: Taotuo's younger brother Wenshi was Attendant Drafting Master of the Palace Secretariat and Administrator of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taotuo's younger brother Wenshi was drafting master of the palace secretariat and prefect of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 義深兄弟七人，多有學尚。

translations.literal: Of Yishen's seven brothers, many had scholarly interests.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yishen's seven brothers, many pursued learning.

sentences.zh: 第二弟同軌以儒學知名。

translations.literal: The second brother, Tonggui, was known for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: The second brother, Tonggui, won renown for Confucian scholarship.

sentences.zh: 第六弟稚廉別有傳。

translations.literal: The sixth brother, Zhilian, has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth brother, Zhilian, is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 義深族弟神威。

translations.literal: Yishen's clansman Shenwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yishen's clansman Shenwei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖融，魏中書侍郎，神威幼有風裁，傳其家業，禮學粗通義訓。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong had been Attendant Master of Writing under Wei; Shenwei from youth showed moral bearing, inherited the family tradition, and had a rough grasp of ritual learning and moral principles.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong had been attendant master of writing under Wei. Shenwei showed moral force even as a boy, carried on the family tradition, and had a working knowledge of ritual and moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 又好音樂，撰集《樂書》，近於百卷。

translations.literal: He also loved music and compiled a Book of Music amounting to nearly a hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved music and compiled a Book of Music running to nearly a hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 魏武之末，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Eastern Wei he was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of Eastern Wei he was left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 天保初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the start of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the opening of the Tianbao reign.

sentences.zh: 贈信州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Xin Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：元忠本自素流，有聞教義，人倫之譽，未以縱橫許之。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Yuanzhong came from an ordinary lineage, known for learning and moral teaching; his repute in human relations was never one that credited him with the arts of stratagem and alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Yuanzhong sprang from a plain family, known for learning and moral teaching — a man whose name in human affairs was never linked to the arts of alliance and intrigue.

sentences.zh: 屬莊帝幽崩，群胡矯擅，士之有志力者皆望勤王之師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang died in mysterious circumstances and the barbarian clique seized power unlawfully, every man of ambition looked for a royal rescue army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang died in shadow and the barbarian faction seized unlawful power, every man of will and talent turned his eyes toward a king's army marching to restore the throne.

sentences.zh: 及高祖東轅，事與心會，一遇雄姿，遂瀝肝膽，以石投水，豈徒然哉？

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor turned his chariot east, purpose and heart aligned; upon meeting that heroic figure he poured out his liver and gall — a stone cast into water, sure to sink without trace. Was that mere chance?
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan turned his chariot east, wish and circumstance met as one; at the first sight of that heroic bearing Yuanzhong poured out his whole heart — a stone thrown into water, bound to sink to the bottom. Could that have been accident alone?

sentences.zh: 既享功名，終知止足，進退之道，有可觀焉。

translations.literal: Having tasted merit and fame, he finally knew when to halt and be content — in the way he advanced and retreated, there is something worth observing.
translations.idiomatic: Having tasted merit and fame, he learned at last where to stop and be satisfied — in how he came forward and stepped back, there is a lesson worth keeping.

sentences.zh: 文偉望重地華，早有志尚，間關夷險之際，終遇英雄之主，雖禮秩未弘，亦為佐命之一。

translations.literal: Wenwei bore noble prestige and radiant lineage; early he had high aspirations. Through hardship and peril he at last met a hero-lord; though rank and honors were never lavish, he still counts among those who helped establish the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei carried weight of birth and bright lineage, and early held high purpose. Through straits and dangers he at last found a lord of heroic stamp; though rank and reward never ran deep, he still belongs among those who helped seat the throne.

sentences.zh: 詢祖詞情艷發，早著聲名，負其才地，肆情矜矯，京華人士，莫不畏其舌端。

translations.literal: Xunzu's literary style blazed with ornament and he won fame early; riding the strength of talent and birth, he gave free rein to pride and affectation — in the capital, none did not fear the edge of his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzu's writing flared with color and he won a name while still young; trusting in talent and station, he indulged pride and display — in the capital, everyone feared the cut of his tongue.

sentences.zh: 任遇未聞，弱年夭逝，若得終介眉壽，通塞未可量焉。

translations.literal: His appointments never rose to great notice; he died young. Had he lived to full white-browed age, who could measure how far he might have risen or fallen?
translations.idiomatic: Preferment never truly found him; he died in early manhood. Had he lived to frost his brows with age, who could say what heights or depths awaited him?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：晉陽、大夏，抱質懷文。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Jinyang and Daxia — holding substance, embracing culture.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Jinyang and Daxia — men who held to substance and carried culture in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 蹈仁履義，咸會風雲。

translations.literal: Walking in benevolence, treading in righteousness, all met the turning of the age.
translations.idiomatic: They walked in benevolence and stood in righteousness, and all alike caught the storm when the age turned.

sentences.zh: 盧嬰貨殖，李厭囂氛。

translations.literal: Lu nurtured commerce and gain; Li disdained the clamor of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Lu turned his hand to trade and profit; Li turned his face from the noise of a corrupt age.

sentences.zh: 始終之操，清濁斯分。

translations.literal: Constancy from first to last — here the pure and the turbid divide.
translations.idiomatic: Constancy from beginning to end — here the clear and the muddy part ways.

sentences.zh: 義深參贊，有謝忠勤。

translations.literal: Yishen served as counselor and aide, yet fell short of devoted loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yishen lent counsel and support, yet fell short of steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
